thread:
morgan: heads up — console showing same service-account key under different orgs for different requests. noticed this in the billing dashboard, looks wrong.
ash: huh, can you paste an example request id?
morgan: request id `req_0a1b2c3d`, key `sa-key-zz15`. sometimes shows org=acme-inc, sometimes org=redwood-eng.
ravi: that sounds like the claim resolver is flapping between SSO mapping and project-binding cache. we had a TTL regression on the claim cache last week.
kevin: we deployed an auth-exchange canary at 02:00 UTC yesterday (deploy-bot: canary-deploy auth-exchange v2.4.1). did you start seeing this after that?
morgan: timeline matches. example token payload from the request that showed acme-inc: `{"sub":"sa-zzz","iss":"sso.acme","claims":{"org":"acme-inc","project":"proj-x"}}` then a subsequent request from same key had `{"org":"redwood-eng"}`.
sarah: is the console showing "claimed org" or "effective org"? I think the UI surface only shows one column currently (we compute effective before rendering).
ravi: backend computes effective org by running route-resolution: prefer explicit project binding -> delegation -> sso claim. cache stores last effective value keyed by service-key. bug in cache invalidation was causing mix of old and new values to be returned under high load.
ash: how would that affect quotas/billing? we attribute tokens to orgs downstream.
kevin: our billing pipeline currently uses the effective org at time-of-ingestion (streaming). if effective flips later, usage can be attributed to the wrong org until we backfill.
sarah: concrete UX idea: show both "claimed org" (from token) and "resolved org" (what we route/attribute to). the console debug view could expose both behind a feature flag.
morgan: agree — we need to make it obvious for customers and support when attribution diverges.
ravi: telemetry change: emit `auth.resolution.path` with values like `project-binding`, `delegation`, `sso-claim`, and also emit `auth.resolution.via_cache:true|false` and `auth.resolution.cache_age_secs`.
ash: +1, that will let us chart how often cache is being used and if stale values cause flips.
kevin: ops note: adding fields to telemetry is fine, but be careful with cardinality. use enums and coarse buckets for cache_age.
sarah: rollout plan: 1) add telemetry and debug columns (hidden) behind `ui/auth-resolution-debug` flag, 2) ship to internal-only for 48h, 3) open to customers as opt-in, 4) after 2 weeks evaluate and flip default.
morgan: what about quota/billing correctness? we should avoid changing attribution logic by default. proposal: pin billing attribution to the first-resolved-org for a token session (30m), and record resolution events so we can re-attribute if customer disputes.
ravi: technically feasible: add `billing_attribution_anchor_ts` and keep original resolved org for that anchor window. we'll need a migration for long-lived tokens.
ash: question: long-lived service accounts could span months. pinning forever might be wrong if ownership legitimately changes.
sarah: we can make anchor window configurable per customer (default 30m) and surface org-change events in admin logs when a change occurs.
kevin: ops + legal check: any compliance concerns if we hold onto previous org attribution? might affect audit trails but should be fine if auditable.
morgan: action items: 1) ravi to open infra bug for cache TTL fix and add a quick mitigation to prefer sso-claim on cache miss (ETA today). 2) sarah to spec UI debug column and flag (ETA EOD). 3) ash to add telemetry event schema PR (link please). 4) kevin to check billing pipeline anchor change for edge cases.
ravi: opened infra bug: https://jira.company/ENG-9999 — included sample logs and repro steps.
sarah: created a console mock and posted screenshot in #design later (will tag). thanks all. :thumbsup:
kevin: leaving a note to watch `billing.attribution.mismatch` alert after rollout. will mute only if false positives are low.
morgan: thanks — marking as blocked until auth-exchange revert or patch; keep me posted.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy completed for auth-exchange v2.4.1 at 2026-03-20T02:00Z (instances: 6/6 healthy)
